sources.authors: Hernán, M. A.; Robins, J. M.
sources.title: Causal Inference: What If
read_sections: Chapters 1–3: counterfactual definitions, randomized experiments, observational studies
sources.protocol_application: Define the intervention, target population, endpoint, assignment mechanism, consistency and no-interference assumptions before evaluation.
sources.transfer_limit: Medical/statistical methods are transferred as experimental-design principles; no claim that software tasks satisfy assumptions automatically.

sources.title: Potential Outcome and Directed Acyclic Graph Approaches to Causality: Relevance for Empirical Practice in Economics
read_sections: Potential-outcome components: units, outcomes, assignment mechanism
Discussion of no interference and individually unobserved counterfactuals
sources.protocol_application: Version-before/after and naturally selected skill users confound assignment; randomized availability is a tractable intervention.
sources.transfer_limit: Population average effects do not identify the cause of an individual failure or a general mechanism.

sources.authors: Howard, S. R.; Ramdas, A.; McAuliffe, J.; Sekhon, J. S.
sources.title: Time-uniform, nonparametric, nonasymptotic confidence sequences
read_sections: Sections 1–2: time-uniform coverage and arbitrary stopping
sources.protocol_application: Fixed-N intervals cannot be repeatedly inspected as if valid at any stopping time; freeze N or choose a valid sequential design in advance.
sources.transfer_limit: An online adaptive agent stream does not automatically meet a confidence sequence’s conditional/martingale assumptions.

sources.authors: Agarwal, R.; Schwarzer, M.; Castro, P. S.; Courville, A. C.; Bellemare, M. G.
sources.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning at the Edge of the Statistical Precipice
read_sections: Section 4: stratified bootstrap intervals, performance profiles, robust aggregate metrics
Table 1 and empirical comparisons across tasks and seeds
sources.protocol_application: Report uncertainty and heterogeneity; preserve task/seed clustering rather than treating repeated runs as independent tasks.
sources.transfer_limit: RL score-normalization and IQM are not copied as substitutes for a predefined binary Hermes success endpoint.

sources.title: AI Agents That Matter
read_sections: Section 2: cost-controlled evaluation and simple retry baselines
Section 5: levels of generality and holdout requirements
sources.protocol_application: Measure actual spending, preparation costs, time, and cost-adjusted baselines; separate example/generalization/family holdouts.
sources.transfer_limit: Complex planning/reflection cannot receive credit for improvements attributable to extra calls or benchmark shortcuts.

sources.title: AgentBench: Evaluating LLMs as Agents
sources.publication: 2023 initial; retrieved v3 text states 4 Oct 2025
read_sections: Execution-outcome categories: CLE, IF, IA, TLE
Appendix J: validity and trajectory analysis
sources.protocol_application: Separate mechanically observed failure categories, difficulty strata, and multi-step tasks; preserve all allocated failures in the denominator.
sources.transfer_limit: Outcome labels and trajectory patterns are not themselves causal root-cause proof.

sources.title: SWE-bench: Can Language Models Resolve Real-World GitHub Issues?
read_sections: Fail-to-pass filtering and patch execution evaluation
sources.protocol_application: Bind evaluation to frozen repository/environment/task snapshots and independently execute postconditions rather than score self-reports.
sources.transfer_limit: Passing repository tests is a bounded benchmark result, not a proof of universal correctness or agent consciousness.
